title: Al-'Asr again: the four
hook: Imam al-Shafi'i said this surah alone would be enough guidance

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-'Asr, the oath by time and the verdict of loss. Your line was by time. Day one hundred seventy-two.

If you could keep only one page of advice for the rest of your life, what would be on it? People argue about this over dinner: one book, one verse, one sentence. Imam al-Shafi'i, the scholar of Islamic law whose name one of the Sunni schools still carries, had an answer about the Qur'an. He's reported to have said that if people reflected on this one surah, it would be enough for them. Three lines.
screen: `ONE PAGE FOR THE REST OF YOUR LIFE.` → `IMAM AL-SHAFI'I.` → `IT WOULD BE ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: The human being is in loss, the surah says. Then the exception, in Pickthall's words: Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance. Four things. First, faith: iman, trust in Allah, the root under everything else. Second, good deeds: 'amal salih, faith that turns into hands. Here, as in other verses, the two come as a pair: belief, and the deeds that show it. Now the surprise. The last two aren't things you do alone. The Arabic word is tawasaw: urge one another, counsel each other, a verb that only works between people. Urge one another to truth, al-haqq: what's right, what's real, even when it's awkward to say. And to patience, as-sabr: endurance, holding steady, not giving up on the right thing when it gets hard. So the way out of loss isn't a private self-improvement plan. It's a small community of people who keep each other honest and keep each other going. It's reported that when two companions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ met, they wouldn't part until one had recited this surah to the other. That's what al-Shafi'i saw in it: belief, action, and two kinds of friendship. The friend who tells you the truth, and the friend who helps you stay the course. Faith, good, truth, patience.
screen: `IMAN — FAITH.` · `'AMAL SALIH — GOOD DEEDS.` · `TAWASAW — URGE ONE ANOTHER.` · `TO TRUTH, AND TO PATIENCE.` · then, large: `FAITH, GOOD, TRUTH, PATIENCE.`

segments.voice: Take the four one at a time, a breath for each: faith, where your trust rests right now; good, one thing you did this week that helped someone; truth, who tells it to you even when it's hard to hear; patience, who helps you keep going. Let a face come for each one. If a place is empty, just notice it.
Al-'Asr again. The four that keep a person from loss: faith, good deeds, urging one another to truth, and to patience. Today's word.
Your line: faith, good, truth, patience. Two of the four only work between people. Day one hundred seventy-two.

howItsDone: Many Muslims know al-'Asr by heart and recite it in the prayers; teachers often use it as a summary of Islamic life, and some friends end a gathering by reciting it together.
